title: Reading Static Pressure with a Manometer
description: The learner reads a U-tube manometer at six points of a supply system (louver, filter, coil, fan, ductwork, diffuser, room) as signed static pressures in in. wg, predicting each before the water levels are revealed, then works out the fan's static pressure rise of 2.50 in. wg.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Reading static pressure with a U-tube manometer
learningObjectives: The learner will interpret U-tube manometer readings taken at six points in a supply system as signed static pressures in inches of water gauge, and infer the fan's static pressure rise, with at least 6 of 7 answers correct.
prerequisites: Air pressure, atmospheric pressure and gauge pressure

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts, slip notes, prompts and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed feedback borders pair with colour; readings carry an explicit + or − sign; the sign is a native radio group (arrow keys); Enter checks and then goes to the next point; keys 1-7 choose a point in Review mode.

controls.label: Sign
controls.purpose: + above room or − below room (not shown for question 7)

controls.label: Reading
controls.purpose: Size of the reading in in. wg; a typed + or − sign also sets the sign

controls.label: Check / Retry (not scored)
controls.purpose: Check the reading (Enter); after a miss, one unscored retry

controls.label: Next point / Go to question 7 / Show summary
Review
controls.purpose: Choose a point to review after question 7 (keys 1-7 or a click on a point also work)

controls.label: Start over

simulation.modelType: Rule table with a derived pressure profile
equations: Reading after an inlet-side part = previous reading − its pressure drop
Fan outlet reading = sum of the discharge-side drops
Fan static pressure rise = outlet reading − inlet reading
rules: Correct when the sign matches and |entered − correct| <= 0.05 in. wg; 0 at point 6 is correct with or without a sign
Seven items in fixed order, one scored attempt each, one unscored retry after a miss
A nonzero reading with no sign, or an entry that is not a number, does not use the attempt
Mastery: 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt
assumptions: Equal air velocity at the fan inlet and outlet (the chapter's simple subtraction)
Water-filled U-tube; each leg moves by half the reading
limitations: Static pressure only; velocity pressure and total pressure are in Chapter 2

sources: Chapter 1 section 'Static Pressure', worked example 'Adding Up a System's Resistance' (illustrative values; the sim labels them 'Illustrative values')

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Committed prediction at each measurement point, then the instrument reading and the reason side by side; the profile builds up on the system drawing
keyQuestions: Is the duct above or below room pressure at this point, and by how much?
Which manometer leg does the water move on when the duct is under suction?
Why does the fan's pressure rise include the suction on its inlet side?
commonMisconceptions: The water rises on the side connected to the duct when the duct is pressurized; in fact it is pushed down on that side.
The fan's pressure rise equals the outlet reading alone, ignoring the suction on the inlet side.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt correct: n of 7'; mastery is 6 of 7 on the first attempt.
The unscored retry and Review mode are not evidence of mastery
